title: 立地競争と最小差別化
sourceLabel: 既存教材をTOEFL形式へ変換 · 元の問1–9に対応
verificationNote: Editorial answers（編集・確認した解答）。元の本文・解説に基づき記述設問を英語4択へ変換しています。元記事の記述問題も引き続き利用できます。

passages.text:
Imagine consumers distributed evenly along a straight street. They buy one unit from the seller that gives them the lowest combined cost: the posted price plus the inconvenience of travel. Suppose first that two sellers offer the same product at the same fixed price. If one seller stands far from the center, moving slightly toward the other can capture consumers in the middle without losing those at the outer end. This strategic pressure can pull both sellers toward a central location.

The result is often associated with Harold Hotelling's 1929 model and the phrase minimum differentiation. The model does not claim that every real business must share one address. It shows how similarity can arise from a specified set of incentives. Each seller chooses a location to enlarge its own market, while consumers collectively might travel less if the sellers were separated. What is stable for competitors under the model can therefore differ from what minimizes total travel.

The conclusion is sensitive to assumptions. If firms can also change prices, a very close location may intensify price competition. If consumers are unevenly distributed, demand has several centers, products differ in quality, relocation is costly, or shoppers value variety, greater separation may be profitable. A circle, a road network, and an online platform also create different notions of distance. The phrase “businesses cluster because of Hotelling's law” is therefore an invitation to identify a mechanism, not a substitute for evidence.

A useful empirical study would compare the model's predictions with observed openings, closures, prices, and customer trips. It would ask whether firms moved toward demand, toward rivals, or toward shared infrastructure such as a station. Competing explanations can produce the same map. The intellectual lesson is broader than retail location: a model earns explanatory force by making its assumptions and testable implications visible.

questions.prompt: What is the main idea of the passage?

options.label: A
options.text: Every business in every market must locate at one central point.

options.label: B
options.text: A location model explains a pressure toward similarity under stated assumptions, and its prediction must be tested against alternatives.

options.label: C
options.text: Consumer travel never matters to a seller's market share.

options.label: D
options.text: Allowing price changes always strengthens clustering.

questions.answer: The model explains a conditional incentive toward similarity and the passage emphasizes testing its assumptions and rival explanations. 正解：B。Aは普遍化、Cは移動負担を否定、Dは近接が価格競争を強めうる記述と逆です。assumptionは「モデルが置く仮定」です。

questions.prompt: Under fixed prices in a linear market, why might a seller near an outer end move slightly toward the center?

options.label: A
options.text: The seller must abandon all outer customers before gaining anyone in the middle.

options.label: B
options.text: The seller can gain consumers near the boundary with the rival while retaining outer-end consumers who still find it closer.

options.label: C
options.text: The move eliminates travel inconvenience for every consumer on the street.

options.label: D
options.text: The rival is legally required to move to the same location.

questions.answer: A small inward move shifts the market boundary toward the rival while outer customers still prefer the nearer seller. 正解：B。Aは外側の客を失わないという条件と逆、Cは全員の移動をゼロにせず、Dは制度的強制ではありません。capture consumersは「消費者を自店の需要として獲得する」です。

questions.prompt: In paragraph 3, “sensitive to assumptions” is closest in meaning to

options.label: A
options.text: A model produces the same conclusion no matter which conditions change.

options.label: B
options.text: Competitors become emotionally disturbed by a model.

options.label: C
options.text: The prediction is likely to change when the model's conditions change.

options.label: D
options.text: The result has been proven without assumptions.

questions.answer: Changing price choice, demand distribution, product quality, relocation costs, or market geometry may change the predicted location. 正解：C。sensitive to assumptionsは「仮定を変えると結論も変わりやすい」です。A・Dは条件依存性を否定し、Bはsensitiveを感情的な意味に誤読しています。

questions.prompt: Why can a location stable for individual sellers differ from one that minimizes consumers' total travel?

options.label: A
options.text: Each seller directly minimizes the travel of every consumer, so the two outcomes must coincide.

options.label: B
options.text: Consumers choose store locations, while sellers have no strategic incentives.

options.label: C
options.text: Each seller seeks to enlarge its own market rather than minimize the sum of all customers' travel distances.

options.label: D
options.text: Total travel depends only on posted prices and never on where sellers stand.

questions.answer: Private incentives and the collective objective are different: each seller maximizes its market, not aggregate travel welfare. 正解：C。中央集中が各社に安定でも、店舗を離した方が総移動距離は短い場合があります。Aは目的の一致を仮定し、B・Dはモデルの設定に反します。aggregateは「全体を合計した」です。

questions.prompt: Why may very close locations be unprofitable when firms can also change prices?

options.label: A
options.text: Close firms are unable to observe one another's prices.

options.label: B
options.text: Consumers stop valuing prices whenever stores are close.

options.label: C
options.text: Relocation costs necessarily fall to zero.

options.label: D
options.text: Proximity can intensify price competition, so profit lost through lower prices may outweigh gains in market access.

questions.answer: When products become close substitutes, firms may cut prices more aggressively, reducing profit. 正解：D。A・Bは価格競争の機構を消し、Cの移転費用ゼロは本文にありません。intensifyは「強める」、outweighは「影響や重要性で上回る」です。

questions.prompt: Why can changing a straight line to a circle or road network alter the model's prediction?

options.label: A
options.text: All geometries give consumers exactly the same routes and market boundaries.

options.label: B
options.text: Different geometries change endpoints, available routes, junctions, and therefore the meaning of distance and firms' best responses.

options.label: C
options.text: A circle prevents consumers from comparing combined costs.

options.label: D
options.text: Road networks make product quality the only relevant variable.

questions.answer: Geometry determines feasible routes and market boundaries: a circle has no endpoints, while a network includes paths and junctions. 正解：B。Aはその違いを否定し、C・Dは本文にない排他的主張です。best responseは「相手の選択に対して自分に最も有利な選択」です。

questions.prompt: Why does the fact that two stores stand near a station NOT prove that one moved toward its rival?

options.label: A
options.text: A station never affects pedestrian demand or access.

options.label: B
options.text: Stores cannot observe where their rivals are located.

options.label: C
options.text: Both stores may independently choose the station for shared infrastructure or concentrated demand, producing the same map through another mechanism.

options.label: D
options.text: A map reveals every firm's motive without information about openings or customer trips.

questions.answer: The same spatial pattern can result from attraction to demand or infrastructure rather than attraction to a competitor. 正解：C。原因を区別するには開店時系列や通行量などが必要です。Aは駅の効果を否定、Bは非現実的、Dは同じ地図を生む複数説明を無視します。infrastructureは「交通・設備などの基盤」です。

questions.prompt: Why does the author call Hotelling's law an “invitation to identify a mechanism”?

options.label: A
options.text: To prevent the model's name from replacing evidence about which assumptions and incentives actually produced the observed clustering

options.label: B
options.text: To claim that naming the law proves every business follows it

options.label: C
options.text: To show that empirical observations are unnecessary once a famous economist is cited

options.label: D
options.text: To argue that only biographical facts about Hotelling can explain store locations

questions.answer: The phrase redirects attention from a label to testable causes and conditions. 正解：A。モデル名は説明の終点ではなく、どのincentive（誘因）が働いたかを問う入口です。B・Cは証拠不要とし、Dは理論を人物伝に置き換えます。mechanismは「観察された結果を生む仕組み」です。

questions.prompt: Which research plan best tests why new cafés choose particular locations?

options.label: A
options.text: Record only current café locations and assume every cluster was caused by rivalry.

options.label: B
options.text: Interview one successful owner and generalize the answer to all openings and closures.

options.label: C
options.text: Compare café names and decoration styles without measuring demand, rent, prices, or feasible sites.

options.label: D
options.text: Combine opening dates and locations with pedestrian flows, rents, station access, rivals' prices, feasible vacant sites, and later closures to test competing explanations.

questions.answer: The design observes choices available at the time and tests rival proximity after controlling for demand and infrastructure. 正解：D。閉店も含めれば開店を成功と誤認しません。Aは原因を仮定、Bは一例の一般化、Cは立地機構の主要変数を欠きます。feasible vacant sitesは「当時実際に選べた空き物件」です。
